threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, close calendar, and responsibilities for the upgraded process.

messages.text:
Kicking off the upgraded quarter-end close planning for project_title: Quarter-End Close and Tax Compliance Process Upgrade.
I have uploaded a first draft of the Quarter-End Close Master Checklist and calendar based on T1 and the roles from T11.
Highlights:
- Target is to complete the close in 7 business days
- Daily activities and owners are mapped in A1
- Escalation paths and cut-off rules are aligned with A5
Please review the checklist structure, the 7-day timeline, and whether the responsibilities per activity look right. I would like to confirm both the calendar and the RACI by tomorrow so we can start socialising with stakeholders.

Thanks for sharing. I went through A1 and the calendar tab.
A couple of observations:
- Day 1 looks quite packed for the bookkeeping team, especially with both bank reconciliations and initial accruals
- The documentation checks linked to A4 are only on Day 5; we might want a lighter pre-check earlier to avoid surprises
On responsibilities, the RACI in A5 for fixed assets and depreciation seems fine to me, but I want to confirm who is on point for coordinating with departments on late submissions.
I can propose a small tweak to the workload distribution if that helps keep us within the 7-day target.

I reviewed the checklist as well.
On the 7-day timeline, it looks achievable if we get supporting documents from cost centre owners on time. The risk section in the project notes about delays from departments is very real for us.
For responsibilities:
- I am comfortable owning the tax-related pre-close checks and helping prepare the list for T8
- For daily bank reconciliations, I suggest we rotate between the bookkeeping team to avoid bottlenecks
One question: in A1, some tasks are marked as shared between bookkeepers without a clear primary owner. Should we assign a single accountable person per task in line with T11?

I had a quick look at the checklist.
The steps make sense to me, but I am not fully sure about the timing for attaching certificates and other documents. Right now I see them grouped later in the week.
If I am assigned some of those tasks, I will need clear guidance from A4 so I do not miss anything.
Also, for the 7-day target, do we already have agreement from the external auditor on when they expect the draft package from A6?

I went through the calendar and I agree with the overall flow.
I can take on:
- Some of the reconciliations on Day 2 and Day 3
- Helping to check that attachments are in place once A4 is final
One concern: the peer review step from T7 is currently on Day 6 only. If we leave all high-risk entries to be reviewed that late, we might struggle if there are corrections. Maybe we can add a lighter review earlier in the week.

Good points on workload and documentation timing.
Proposal:
- Move part of the accruals work from Day 1 to Day 2, keeping only the most material items on Day 1
- Add a quick documentation spot-check on Day 3 focused on high-value entries, using the draft standards from A4
On responsibilities for late submissions, I suggest we make one bookkeeper the primary contact per department, with me as escalation if deadlines slip.
If you are ok with that, I will update A1 and A5 accordingly.

Agree that each task in A1 should have a single accountable owner, even if several people contribute.
Let us do this:
- Assign one primary owner per checklist line in line with T11
- Keep a separate column for backup support
On the tax pre-close checks and the list for T8, thanks for volunteering. I will reflect that in the RACI in A5.
I will share an updated version of A1 later today with these ownership changes.

On the 7-day target and auditor expectations: we have an informal agreement that they receive the draft package from A6 by end of Day 7. I will confirm the exact timing with them, but we should plan as if Day 7 is firm.
For documentation and certificates, A4 will spell out what needs to be attached and where. In A1, I will:
- Spread the attachment tasks across Days 2 to 5
- Add a clear owner for each attachment group
We will also cover this in the pre-close training linked to T9 so everyone is comfortable with the steps.

I like the idea of moving some accruals to Day 2 and adding a Day 3 documentation spot-check.
For department coordination, I can take responsibility for the operations cost centres and keep a simple log of late items that we can feed into A8 for the compliance review.
Once you update A1 and A5, I can sanity-check the workload distribution for the bookkeeping team.

On the peer review timing, I agree we should not leave everything to Day 6.
Maybe we can:
- Flag high-risk entries as we go, using the criteria from T7
- Do a short review window on Day 3 and Day 5, then a final sweep on Day 6
That way, if we find issues, we still have time to correct them without pushing the close beyond 7 days.

The single accountable owner per task approach works for me.
For clarity, I can draft a quick mapping of:
- Bank reconciliations
- Fixed asset updates and depreciation checks
- Tax pre-close checks
and suggest primary owners for each, then you can plug that into A1 and A5.
I will share that by tomorrow morning.

Understood on the Day 7 expectation.
Spreading the attachment tasks across the week will help. Once A4 is final and A1 is updated, I would appreciate a short walkthrough during the T9 training so I can double-check I am following the right steps.
I am ok to be primary owner for some of the attachment tasks if the instructions are clear.

Agreed on spreading the peer reviews.
I will adjust A1 so that:
- High-risk entries are tagged as we post them
- We have review slots on Days 3, 5, and 6, aligned with the checklist from A7 and T7
This should reduce last-minute surprises and help us keep the 7-day close intact.

I have now updated A1 and A5 with:
- The rebalanced workload across Days 1 to 7
- Single accountable owners per task, with backups
- Distributed documentation and peer review steps
Before we lock this in, can each of you confirm that your assigned tasks and timing are workable? If there are no strong objections, I would like to formally adopt this calendar and the 7-day completion target for the next quarter-end close.

I have checked my assignments in A1 and they look reasonable.
With the adjustments you made, I believe the 7-day close is realistic, assuming departments respect the submission deadlines.
From my side, I am fine to proceed with this calendar and the responsibilities as documented in A5.

I reviewed my tasks as well.
The timing for reconciliations, tax checks, and support on T8 is fine for me. The RACI in A5 is clear.
I support adopting the 7-day calendar and the defined responsibilities.

From my side, the updated schedule works.
The split of reconciliations and peer review slots is manageable, and the attachment checks I am assigned to are spread out enough.
I am ok with the 7-day target and the responsibilities as they stand.

I checked my tasks in A1.
The attachment and documentation steps look clear enough for me, especially knowing we will cover them again in T9.
I am comfortable with the 7-day close plan and my responsibilities.

Thanks everyone for reviewing.
Based on your confirmations, we will:
- Approve the quarter-end close calendar with the 7 business day completion target
- Confirm the roles and responsibilities as documented in A1 and A5, aligned with T1 and T11
I will share the final links in the channel and inform the external stakeholders of the new timeline.

threads.thread_goal: Define standards for journal entries and supporting documentation.

messages.text:
Following up on the calendar, I have drafted:
- Standard journal entry templates for recurring transactions as part of T2
- A first version of documentation and attachment standards aligned with T5
The templates cover payroll, depreciation, accruals, and provisions, and are linked to the checklist in A7 for high-risk entries.
The documentation standards draft is in A4, with required supporting documents, naming conventions, and storage rules.
Please review and comment on:
1) Any missing fields or examples in the templates
2) Whether the attachment rules are practical for your day-to-day work
We should aim to finalise these before the next close so they can be used end to end.

I reviewed the templates for payroll and depreciation.
They look solid overall. A couple of suggestions:
- For payroll, add a field for headcount or FTE count so we can reconcile to HR reports
- For depreciation, include a reference to the asset ID from A3 to make it easier to trace back to the fixed asset register
On A4, the list of required documents is clear. I like that we have separate rules for recurring vs one-off entries.
I think these templates are close to ready for use in the next close.

I checked the accruals and provisions templates.
They are straightforward, but I wonder if we should add a standard way to document the calculation logic, maybe a short narrative field or a link to a supporting sheet.
On A4, I like the naming convention, but I am not sure if everyone will remember all the codes. Maybe we can include a quick reference table in A4 and also link it from A1 so people can find it easily during the close.

I went through A4 and the templates.
The structure helps, but I am a bit unsure about which certificates go with which type of entry, especially for tax-related items.
Would it be possible to add a simple example per transaction type, maybe one screenshot or short description, so it is easier to follow?
Also, for the naming convention, I will probably need that quick reference table mentioned above.

I have reviewed the templates and A4 from a control perspective.
They align well with our accounting policies and should help with auditability.
A few control-related tweaks:
- For high-risk entries, the template should include a field to capture who performed the peer review and the date, consistent with A7 and T7
- For tax-sensitive entries, we should reference the relevant section of A2 or the tax rule applied
Once we incorporate these, I am comfortable using these templates in the next close, but I would like to hear if anyone sees practical issues before we formalise that.

Thanks for the feedback.
I will:
- Add a headcount/FTE field to the payroll template
- Include an asset ID field and a direct link to A3 in the depreciation template
That should make reconciliations and audits smoother.
Once I update these, I will flag the new version of T2 as ready for final review.

Good call on documenting the calculation logic.
I will add a standard narrative field in the accruals and provisions templates, plus an optional link field for a supporting workbook.
For the naming convention, I will extend A4 with a quick reference table and ask to have a link from A1 so it is easy to find during the close.

On the examples, that makes sense.
I will add one simple example per transaction type in A4, including which certificates or documents to attach and where to store them.
We can also walk through a couple of cases during the T9 training so everyone is comfortable using the standards.

I agree with adding the reviewer and date fields for high-risk entries.
That will make it easier to prove the peer review happened when auditors look at A7.
Referencing A2 for tax-sensitive entries is also helpful. Maybe we can include a short dropdown in the template with the main tax rule categories so people do not have to type free text every time.

From a practical standpoint, the extra fields you suggest are fine for me.
As long as the templates are pre-filled where possible, it should not slow us down too much.
I would just ask that we keep the instructions in A4 concise so people can quickly check what is needed without reading long text.

Examples in A4 and a walkthrough in T9 will help a lot.
With that in place, I feel more confident that I can use the templates correctly and attach the right certificates.
I do not have any other changes to suggest.

I have now:
- Added reviewer name and date fields to the high-risk entry templates, aligned with A7 and T7
- Included a reference field for the relevant tax rule, with a dropdown of main categories linked to A2
- Updated A4 with the quick reference table, examples, and concise instructions
From my side, T2 and T5 are ready for sign-off, but I want to confirm that everyone is comfortable using these from the next close onward.

I am comfortable with the updated templates and A4.
They cover the main recurring entries we use and should reduce back-and-forth with auditors.
I support adopting these templates and documentation standards starting from the next quarter-end close.

I am ok with using these templates and standards from the next close.
The extra fields are manageable, and the examples in A4 make it clear what to attach.
No further comments from me.

With the examples and the quick reference in A4, I am fine to start using these templates in the next close.
I might still have questions during the first run, but the structure is clear enough for me to follow.

Thanks for the updates and feedback.
From a control and compliance standpoint, the templates in T2 and the standards in T5 and A4 look good.
We will:
- Use these standard journal entry templates for recurring transactions from the next quarter-end close
- Apply the documentation and attachment standards in A4 to all entries, with peer review captured via A7 and T7
I will communicate this change in the pre-close training session under T9.

threads.thread_goal: Validate tax and depreciation schedules and align with tax advisor.

messages.text:
I have uploaded the updated Tax Calculation and Reconciliation Workbook and the latest Fixed Asset Depreciation Schedule for this quarter.
These correspond to T3 and T4 and are stored as A2 and A3.
Key updates:
- Tax rates and thresholds refreshed per current legislation
- Sample calculations tested against prior quarter figures
- Depreciation methods and useful lives aligned across ledgers
I would like you to:
1) Sanity-check the depreciation schedule in A3 against recent asset movements
2) Review the main tax calculations in A2 for reasonableness
We also need to prepare the list of complex items for T8 before we speak with the tax advisor.
Please share any issues or questions before we sign off for this quarter.

I have gone through A3 and spot-checked a few assets.
Findings:
- The useful lives and methods look consistent with our policy
- For two recently disposed assets, I see they are still marked as active; we should probably update their status and ensure no depreciation is booked this quarter
On A2, the main corporate tax calculation reconciles well to the trial balance. I would like to double-check the deferred tax section, but overall it looks reasonable.
I can also start drafting the list of complex items for T8 based on the adjustments tab in A2.

I checked a sample of smaller assets in A3.
The depreciation amounts tie back to the general ledger for the items I tested.
I am less comfortable reviewing the more complex tax calculations in A2, but I can help verify that the totals match the GL and that the rates used match the summary tab.
If there are specific sections you want me to focus on, let me know.

I had a look at A3.
The layout is clear, but I am not entirely sure how to confirm if the depreciation for each asset is correct beyond checking totals.
If you can point me to a simple check I can do, I am happy to help with some spot checks.
On A2, I can help verify that the final tax expense and payable match the entries we plan to post.

I reviewed the tax rates and thresholds in A2.
They match the latest legislation I am aware of, and the sample calculations vs prior quarter look consistent.
For depreciation in A3, I agree with the comments about the disposed assets; we should clean those up before sign-off.
For T8, I suggest we flag:
- Any large one-off adjustments
- Changes in tax rules applied this quarter
- Items where the tax base differs significantly from the accounting base
I can help compile this list once we finalise the checks on A2 and A3.

Thanks for catching the disposed assets in A3.
I will:
- Update their status to disposed
- Reverse any depreciation that may have been calculated for this quarter
On the deferred tax section in A2, I will walk through the main movements and add a short explanation tab so it is easier to follow.
Once that is done, it would be great if you could confirm that the movements align with the temporary differences schedule.

For your review, focusing on:
- Matching the totals in A2 to the GL
- Checking that the rates in the summary tab are applied correctly in the detailed calculations
would be very helpful.
I will also highlight a few sections where we had changes vs last quarter so you can pay extra attention there.

For A3, a simple check you can do is:
- Pick a few assets
- Verify cost, useful life, and method
- Recalculate the quarterly depreciation using the formula in the header
If your result matches the schedule, we gain extra comfort.
On A2, confirming that the final tax expense and payable match the planned journal entries will also be useful.
I will mark a few assets for you to test so it is easier to start.

Once you update A3 for the disposed assets, please ping me.
I will then:
- Re-run the reconciliation of total depreciation to the GL
- Check that the temporary differences in A2 reflect the updated depreciation
After that, I can finalise the draft list of complex items for T8, focusing on deferred tax and any unusual adjustments.

I have now checked the totals in A2 against the GL and the rates in the summary tab.
Everything ties for the sections I reviewed.
I did not see any obvious issues, but I left a couple of comments where the narrative could be clearer, especially around one-off adjustments.

I followed your steps on A3 for a few assets.
My recalculations matched the schedule, so that gives me more confidence in the numbers.
On A2, I checked that the final tax expense and payable match the planned journal entries in the checklist, and they do.
I did not find any issues beyond what has already been mentioned.

I have now:
- Updated A3 for the disposed assets and re-run the totals
- Added an explanation tab in A2 for deferred tax movements
- Reviewed the comments and cleared any open questions
From my perspective, both A2 and A3 are technically sound and aligned with our policies.
Before we sign off, are there any remaining concerns from your side?

I rechecked A3 and the reconciliation after your updates.
The disposed assets are now correctly excluded, and the total depreciation matches the GL.
In A2, the deferred tax explanation tab makes the movements much clearer, and I do not see any inconsistencies with the temporary differences.
From my side, I am comfortable treating both A2 and A3 as final for this quarter.

I agree with the conclusions.
The tax rates and calculations in A2 look correct, and the depreciation schedule in A3 is consistent with our asset records.
I suggest we now finalise the list of complex items for T8 and schedule the session with the tax advisor to confirm the treatments.
Assuming no objections from them, I am fine signing off A2 for this quarter.

No further concerns from me.
The checks I did on A2 and A3 still hold after your updates.
I am ok with treating the depreciation schedule as final and using the tax workbook as the basis for the quarter-end entries.

I do not have any additional comments.
The guidance you gave helped me understand the checks better, and I did not find any issues in the samples I reviewed.
I am ok with moving forward with these schedules.

Thanks for all the reviews.
We will:
- Treat the Fixed Asset Depreciation Schedule in A3 as final and ready to post
- Use the updated Tax Calculation and Reconciliation Workbook in A2 as the basis for this quarter, subject to confirmation from the tax advisor under T8
I will prepare the complex items list for T8 using your inputs and book one of the available slots with the tax advisor to confirm the treatments.

threads.thread_goal: Run and debrief the trial close using the new checklist.

messages.text:
We have completed the trial run of the new close checklist on last month data as part of T10.
Summary from A1 and the timings log:
- Total duration: effectively 6 business days, but with some late evenings
- Biggest bottlenecks: collecting supporting documents from departments and peer review of high-risk entries
- Documentation compliance: a few missing attachments, captured in A8
I have logged the main issues and suggestions in the T10 notes and A8.
Let us use this thread to:
1) Share what worked well and what did not
2) Decide which adjustments we want to make to A1 before the real quarter-end close
3) Confirm how we will track exceptions for T12 during the actual close.

From my side, the structure in A1 helped a lot; it was clear what needed to be done each day.
What did not work so well:
- Some departments still sent documents late, which compressed our time for reviews
- The peer review slots were sometimes overloaded because several high-risk entries landed at the same time
For T12, I suggest we use A8 actively during the close to log any checklist steps that are delayed or skipped, plus any documentation gaps, so we can summarise them easily afterwards.

I agree that A1 gave good visibility.
The main pain point for me was chasing attachments and certificates. Even with A4, some departments were not sure what to send, so we had to go back and forth.
Maybe we can send a short pre-close reminder to cost centre owners with a link to A4 and a simple deadline calendar.
On peer reviews, I think we need a clearer rule on when to tag an entry as high-risk so we do not over-tag and overload the reviewers.

For me, the checklist in A1 was helpful, but I struggled a bit with the timing of documentation tasks.
Sometimes I realised late that a certificate was missing and had to rush to get it.
If we can add clearer reminders in A1 for when to check attachments, that would help.
I also found it useful that we logged issues in A8; it made it easier to remember what went wrong.

Thanks for running the trial and capturing the data in T10 and A8.
From a management view, the fact that we finished in 6 days is encouraging, but the late evenings are a red flag.
I see three areas to adjust in A1:
1) Stronger pre-close communication to departments, with clear deadlines and escalation
2) Slightly earlier cut-off for high-risk entries so peer reviews are not all at the end
3) More explicit documentation checkpoints, tied to A4
Let us discuss concrete changes we want to make before we lock the checklist for the real close.

On the attachments side, I agree that some departments were unsure.
We could:
- Create a short one-page summary from A4 tailored for cost centre owners
- Send it with a pre-close reminder email two days before the close, including their specific deadlines from A1
For high-risk tagging, we can refine the criteria in A7 and T7 so that only material or complex entries are flagged, not every adjustment.

For the earlier cut-off on high-risk entries, I suggest we:
- Set Day 5 as the last day to post new high-risk entries, except for emergencies
- Reserve Day 6 mainly for peer review and corrections
We can reflect this in A1 and in the criteria in A7.
For T12, I can draft a simple structure in A8 to categorise exceptions by type: timing, documentation, calculation, etc.

The one-page summary for cost centre owners sounds very helpful.
If we keep it simple and highlight the most common document types, I think it will reduce the back-and-forth.
I also like the idea of tightening the high-risk criteria in A7; during the trial, I probably tagged a few entries that did not really need full peer review.

Clearer documentation checkpoints in A1 would help me a lot.
If we can add a specific step each day to confirm that attachments are in place for the entries posted that day, I am less likely to miss something.
I also support sending reminders to departments with the summary from A4; that should make it easier for them to know what to send.

I like the Day 5 cut-off for new high-risk entries.
We can document that in A1 and in the playbook A5 as a formal rule, with exceptions requiring my approval.
On T12 and A8, categorising exceptions by type will make it easier to spot patterns and propose improvements after the close.

Based on the trial and your feedback, here are the concrete adjustments I propose for A1:
1) Add daily documentation checkpoints tied to A4, with clear owners
2) Introduce a Day 5 cut-off for new high-risk entries, with Day 6 focused on peer review and corrections
3) Add a pre-close communication step to departments, referencing the one-page summary from A4 and their deadlines
4) Link A8 directly from A1 so exceptions can be logged in real time for T12
If we agree on these, I will update A1 and the related sections in A5 and A7.

Those adjustments capture the main lessons from T10.
I support updating A1, A5, and A7 accordingly and using A8 as the live log for exceptions during the real close.
This should make it easier to compile the T12 report afterwards.

I agree with the proposed changes.
Daily documentation checkpoints and the Day 5 cut-off for high-risk entries should reduce last-minute pressure.
I am ok with using A8 during the close to log any issues I encounter.

The adjustments sound good to me.
The daily documentation checkpoints will help me stay on top of attachments, and having A8 linked directly from A1 will make it easier to record any problems.
I do not have any additional changes to suggest.

I am aligned with these adjustments.
They address the main risks we saw in the trial while keeping the overall 7-day structure intact.
Let us proceed with updating A1, A5, and A7 as proposed and use A8 as the central log for T12 during the real close.
We will treat these changes as the updated baseline for the upcoming quarter-end.

threads.thread_goal: Prepare final quarter-end package and confirm readiness for auditors.

messages.text:
We are approaching quarter-end, and I have prepared the Draft Quarter-End Financial Statements Package as part of T6.
The package is stored as A6 and includes:
- Draft balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow
- Key variance analysis vs prior quarter
- Links to supporting schedules such as A2, A3, and A8
Before we send this to the external auditors, I need your help to:
1) Review your areas for obvious errors or missing explanations
2) Check that the documentation and certificates are in place per A4
3) Confirm that any exceptions logged in A8 are reflected in the draft T12 report
Please add comments directly in A6 and summarise any major points here.

I have reviewed the income statement and the tax-related notes in A6.
Observations:
- The tax expense reconciles to A2 and the effective tax rate is in line with expectations
- One variance vs prior quarter on other operating expenses could use a short explanation, as it is mainly driven by a one-off provision
I also checked that the main tax certificates are attached according to A4, and they look complete.
In A8 and the draft T12 content, the tax-related exceptions are correctly captured with remediation actions.

I checked the balance sheet sections I worked on.
The reconciliations tie to the GL, and the supporting documents are attached as per A4.
I noticed one small mismatch in the fixed asset note vs A3, which I have commented on in A6; it looks like a rounding difference.
In A8, the exceptions I logged around late department submissions are present, and the T12 draft mentions the follow-up actions.

I reviewed a few notes in A6 and checked that the certificates I was responsible for are attached.
Using A4 as a guide, I confirmed that the main entries I posted have the right documents.
I did not spot any major issues, but I left a comment on one note where I was not sure if an additional explanation was needed for a small variance.

I focused on the cash flow statement and the reconciliation notes in A6.
The cash flow ties back to the balance sheet movements, and the main reconciling items are explained.
I also checked that the peer-reviewed high-risk entries documented via A7 are properly reflected in the notes where relevant.
In A8, the documentation-related exceptions are summarised clearly, and the T12 draft picks them up with remediation timelines.

Thanks for the review.
I will add a short explanation in A6 for the other operating expenses variance, referencing the one-off provision.
Good to hear that the tax certificates and the tax-related items in A8 and T12 are consistent.
If you see any other notes that could benefit from a brief narrative, please flag them.

I saw your comment on the fixed asset note.
I will reconcile the note to A3 and adjust for the rounding difference so that the figures match exactly.
Thanks for confirming that the late submission exceptions in A8 and T12 are correctly captured.

Appreciate you checking the certificates.
I will review the note you commented on in A6 and decide whether we need an extra line of explanation; for small variances, a brief mention is usually enough.
If anything is unclear, I will adjust the wording before we send the package to the auditors.

I also checked the link between the cash flow in A6 and the tax payments schedule in A2.
The amounts line up, and the timing of payments is consistent with the notes.
From my side, the statements and notes now give a coherent picture for the auditors.

One more small point: in A6, the disclosure about the new close process could mention that we implemented the peer review checklist A7 and the documentation standards A4.
That might help the auditors understand the control improvements this quarter.

Good idea.
We can add a short paragraph in the notes in A6 summarising the process upgrades, referencing A1, A4, A7, and A8, and pointing to the playbook A5.
That should give auditors context without overloading the statements.

Agreed.
I will add a concise note in A6 describing the key process improvements and referencing the relevant artifacts.
This will also help frame any questions they may have during the audit and tax Q and A.

I have now:
- Addressed the comments in A6 on variances and rounding
- Confirmed that A2, A3, and the main certificates per A4 reconcile to the draft statements
- Ensured that all exceptions in A8 are reflected in the draft T12 report with remediation actions
From my perspective, the package is ready to go to the auditors.
Before we formally approve it, can each of you confirm that you are comfortable with the sections you reviewed?

I rechecked the income statement and tax notes after your updates.
Everything looks consistent, and the additional explanation on the one-off provision is clear.
I am comfortable with the sections I reviewed and support sending A6 to the auditors.

I confirm that the balance sheet sections and related notes I reviewed are accurate after your adjustments.
The fixed asset note now matches A3, and the new process disclosure reads well.
I am ok with submitting A6 to the auditors.

I am comfortable with the parts I checked.
The certificates I handled are attached correctly, and the note I asked about is now clearer.
No objections from me to sending the package.

I confirm that the cash flow statement and related reconciliations in A6 are accurate after your final tweaks.
The references to A7 and A8 in the notes are also clear.
From my side, the package is ready for the auditors.

Thanks for all the checks.
Based on your confirmations, we will:
- Approve the Draft Quarter-End Financial Statements Package in A6 for submission to the external auditors
- Use A8 and the final T12 report to track any findings and remediation actions that come out of the audit
I will send A6 to the auditors today and keep this channel updated on any questions they raise.
